diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $f, g \in H^{\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)$ with $\alpha \geq 0$.
The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted pointwise Leibniz inequality is false. For example, at alpha=2 take f=1 and a smooth periodic g at a point where -Delta g<0. Since C(2)=2, the inequality becomes -Delta g <= 2(-Delta g), which fails there. At alpha=0 it similarly becomes fg <= 2fg and fails wherever fg<0. Moreover, the stated H^alpha hypotheses do not ensure the L-infinity quantities in the claimed norm consequence are finite. The nonlinear energy estimate later invokes this false lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false pointwise statement with a valid fractional Leibniz/commutator estimate under appropriate Sobolev and L-infinity hypotheses, and redo the nonlinear energy estimate including all commutator terms.
issues.overall_effect: The principal uniform high-Sobolev estimate for the Galerkin solutions, and hence the convergence, existence, and spatial-error arguments that use it, are not proved as written.
issues.title: False pointwise fractional product inequality
issues.why_classification: A standard type of replacement estimate may preserve the intended method, but it requires a contained nontrivial lemma and a new nonlinear energy calculation rather than a local correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $u_0\in H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}(\Omega)$, where $\alpha\in[1,2]$.
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Sobolev embedding $H^{1+\alpha}(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$:
\frac{d}{dt} \|v\|^2  \leq \frac{1}{4} \|\partial_{x_1}(\bar{u} + \bar{w})\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \|v\|^2 \leq C \|v\|^2

issues.failure_explanation: Both the high-order energy estimate and uniqueness argument require uniform control of a first derivative in L-infinity by the H^{1+alpha} norm. In two dimensions this control is available when 1+alpha>2, but not at the included endpoint alpha=1, where the assumed space is only H^2. The cited embedding into L-infinity controls the function, not its derivative. The inverse inequality stated earlier would introduce an N-dependent factor and cannot supply the uniform estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a new endpoint energy and uniqueness argument that avoids W^{1,infinity} control, or strengthen the endpoint data and solution regularity beyond H^2; otherwise exclude alpha=1 from these results.
issues.overall_effect: Local uniform H^2 control, uniqueness, convergence of the full Galerkin sequence, and the spectral error proof are unsupported for the advertised alpha=1 endpoint.
issues.title: Endpoint alpha=1 lacks the derivative L-infinity control used throughout
issues.why_classification: The source supplies no endpoint argument. The evident repairs either require substantially new analysis or withdraw/change the central alpha=1 regularity regime advertised by the paper.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \norm{u_{N}(\cdot,t)} &\leq C,
\norm{u_{N}(\cdot,t)}_{1+\alpha} &\leq C,

issues.failure_explanation: Equicontinuity and boundedness in the infinite-dimensional space L2 do not imply relative compactness in C([0,T];L2). The proof omits the required pointwise relative compactness argument. The available H^{1+alpha} bound could provide it through compact Sobolev embedding, but that step is not made.

failure_location.quote: Combined with the uniform boundedness in $L^2_{\text{per}}(\Omega)$ from \eqref{bd1}, the Arzelà-Ascoli theorem guaranties the existence of a subsequence $\{u_{N_k}\}$ that converges uniformly to some function $\bar{u}$ in $C([0,\bar{T}]; L^2_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke and verify the compact embedding H^{1+alpha}(Omega) compactly into L2(Omega), use bd3 to establish pointwise relative compactness, and then apply the Banach-valued Arzela-Ascoli theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted strongly and uniformly convergent subsequence does not follow from the argument stated, so the subsequent passage to the nonlinear limit is incomplete.
issues.title: Arzela-Ascoli is applied without establishing pointwise compactness in L2
issues.why_classification: Assuming the claimed uniform H^{1+alpha} bound is valid, the missing compactness step is short, standard, and preserves all conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a finite time $\bar T$ such that the following bounds hold
\bar T := \frac{T_b}{2} = \frac{1}{C\sqrt{D_0}},
The crucial observation is that the existence time $\bar{T}$ depends on $\|u_0\|_{1+\alpha}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Bound bd3 is proved only up to the local time bar T and is not uniform for all time. On restarting, the new H^{1+alpha} norm may be larger, so the next guaranteed lifespan may shrink; the argument gives no lower bound on the sum of continuation intervals and no global a priori H^{1+alpha} estimate. L2 conservation does not supply the missing high-norm bound.

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a global H^{1+alpha} a priori bound or another continuation criterion that prevents finite-time blow-up, or weaken the theorem to local existence.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed global-in-time strong existence and uniqueness for every T>=0 is not established; only a local result is potentially supported.
issues.title: Local bounds do not justify global continuation
issues.why_classification: The available resolution either requires new global well-posedness architecture or abandons the theorem's global-time guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While the adaptation from the one-dimensional Kawahara setting to our multidimensional fractional ZK equation requires careful handling of the fractional Laplacian and the additional spatial dimension, the core analytical techniques remain applicable.

For brevity and to maintain focus on the novel aspects of our spectral discretization for the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK}, we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology.

issues.failure_explanation: The source proves only L2 coercivity of an N-dependent, non-self-adjoint discrete form. It supplies none of the stability, fractional regularity, duality, or approximation estimates needed to deduce the N-uniform H^l bound. It expressly acknowledges that passing from a one-dimensional integer-order problem to a two-dimensional fractional operator requires additional work and then omits that work.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish N-uniform stability and approximation estimates for the actual two-dimensional fractional modified projection, including the required dual regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The main O(N^{-r}) projection estimate, and consequently the claimed optimal spatial convergence theorem, lack their essential analytical foundation.
issues.title: Core modified-projection approximation theorem is left unproved
issues.why_classification: This is the central new lemma behind the advertised optimal rate, and proving it requires substantial new analysis rather than a local completion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $u \in C^1([0,T]; C^1(\Omega))$, $w \in C^1([0,T]; H^r_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$
The proofs of Theorem \ref{thm:proj_error} and Lemma \ref{lem:time_error} follow the approach developed by Deng \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the Kawahara equation.

issues.failure_explanation: Because the defining operator depends on the time-dependent coefficient u, differentiating the projection equation introduces terms involving u_t and the projection error. Controlling these terms with the asserted N-uniform H^l rate requires a nontrivial stability argument. No such argument is given, and the cited omitted projection methodology does not establish it within the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the defining variational problem and prove an N-uniform stability estimate for the resulting equation, using explicit bounds on u_t and the already established projection error.
issues.overall_effect: The time-projection term in the spectral error equation is uncontrolled, so the Gronwall estimate for the algebraic spatial rate does not follow.
issues.title: Time-differentiated modified-projection estimate is unsupported
issues.why_classification: If a valid modified-projection stability theory is supplied, this is a contained but nontrivial additional lemma; it does not by itself require changing the advertised rate.

Assume that $u$ is the exact solution of \eqref{eqn:fZK} satisfying $u \in C^1([0,T]; H^r_{\text{per}}(\Omega))$ with $r \geq \alpha + 1$

issues.failure_explanation: The exponential projection estimate invoked in the proof requires the functions being projected, and for the time-error term their time derivatives, to have uniform analytic regularity. The theorem assumes only fixed Sobolev regularity of the solution and analyticity of u0. The paper proves no propagation of analyticity from u0 to u(t), nor uniform analytic bounds on [0,T].

failure_location.quote:
If, in addition, the initial data \(u_0\) is real-analytic, then there exist positive constants \(C\) and \(\sigma\), independent of \(N\), such that
\[
\|u(t)-u_N(t)\|\le C\,\mathrm{e}^{-\sigma N},
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume and quantify uniform spatial analyticity of the exact solution and the required time derivative throughout [0,T], or prove propagation of analyticity with uniform bounds from the analytic initial data.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential-in-N convergence conclusion is unsupported under the theorem's stated assumptions, although the algebraic conclusion is a separate matter.
issues.title: Analytic initial data is insufficient for the exponential spatial estimate used
issues.why_classification: The exponential rate can remain intact after a substantial but localized hypothesis strengthening or an additional analyticity-propagation result; the algebraic theorem need not be abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t} = e^{-L t} \mathcal{N}\left( e^{L t} V(t) \right) =: \mathcal{F}(t, V(t)).
Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$, completing the proof of the local error estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: The generic RK4 Taylor expansion proves order five for each fixed finite-dimensional system only when the needed derivatives of F are bounded. Here time derivatives of F differentiate e^{±Lt}; since L has frequencies of size N^{alpha+1}, these derivatives can grow with N. The proof gives no commutator estimates or derivative-count calculation showing that r>=alpha+5 controls the fourth total derivative uniformly in N. The final assertion of uniformity is therefore unsupported.

\]
where the constant $C$ depends on $\|u_0\|_{r}$, $\alpha$, and the final time $T$, but is independent of $\Delta t$ and $N$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive uniform bounds for all solution and transformed-vector-field derivatives entering the fifth-order remainder, with whatever additional Sobolev regularity is actually required, or allow an explicitly N-dependent local-error constant.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed N-independent local temporal error, which is needed to combine time and space errors uniformly, has not been proved.
issues.title: Uniform-in-N RK4 local error constant is not established by the regularity assumption
issues.why_classification: A contained high-regularity commutator and derivative analysis may restore fourth-order time accuracy, but it is nontrivial and may require strengthening the stated regularity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the linearized fZK equation with $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, the integrating-factor RK4 scheme is stable under the condition
We now analyze the temporal truncation error of the integrating-factor RK4 scheme \eqref{eq:rk4_update} applied to the transformed system \eqref{transsys}.

issues.failure_explanation: A local O(Delta t^5) defect does not by itself imply a global O(Delta t^4) error. One also needs zero-stability/nonlinear Lipschitz control and a discrete error recursion with constants uniform in N under a suitable timestep condition. The only stability theorem treats a constant-coefficient linearized equation, not the quadratic transformed system, and no nonlinear stability analysis is supplied.

failure_location.quote:
The global error accumulates as $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^4)$ over $\mathcal{O}(1/\Delta t)$ time steps. Combining with the spatial error analysis from Theorem \ref{thm:spectral_accuracy}, the overall error of the fully discrete scheme satisfies
\[
\|u(t_n) - u_N^n\| \leq C_1 N^{-r} + C_2 \Delta t^4,
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove nonlinear stability for the integrating-factor RK4 iterates, derive a uniform discrete Gronwall estimate, and state the necessary timestep restriction and regularity assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The stated fully discrete error bound and the claimed optimal fourth-order temporal convergence are unsupported.
issues.title: Local truncation error is converted to a global fully discrete estimate without nonlinear stability
issues.why_classification: Establishing the fully discrete guarantee requires a new nonlinear stability and global-error analysis, not merely completion of the local Taylor calculation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: u(x,y,t) = 3c \sech^2\left(\frac{\sqrt{c}}{2}\left[(x - ct)\cos\theta + y\sin\theta\right]\right),
We consider a solitary wave with amplitude parameter $c=1$ propagating along the x-axis ($\theta=0$) over the time interval $t\in[0,10]$ on the spatial domain $\Omega = [-20\pi, 20\pi]^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The sech-squared profile is a whole-space line solitary wave, not a periodic function on the stated finite torus. For theta=0 its values and derivatives at x=-20pi and x=20pi are generally unequal once the center is displaced, so it does not satisfy the boundary conditions of the numerical problem. It also is independent of y and hence is not a two-dimensionally localized wave packet. Errors against it therefore include an unquantified periodic-domain truncation mismatch.

failure_location.quote: This example serves to validate the theoretical framework developed in Sections \ref{sec3}-\ref{sec5} by examining the classical ZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK} with $\alpha=2$, for which exact analytical solitary wave solutions are known.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe the profile as an approximate large-domain reference and quantify the periodic boundary/truncation error, or replace it with a genuinely periodic exact solution or an independently converged numerical reference.
issues.overall_effect: The experiment does not provide an exact-solution validation of the periodic scheme or a clean verification of its asymptotic spatial error as claimed.
issues.title: The purported exact solitary-wave reference violates the periodic problem
issues.why_classification: The numerical method itself need not change, but the validation claim requires a corrected reference construction or a limited weakening with boundary-error analysis.
